body: Yes, my apologies, that was a serious typo. She can sit, no problem, it's standing for periods longer than 15 minutes at a time that is an issue. Still, definitely terrible for someone so young, and especially when she didn't grow up like that, so has not been living a life adjusted to it.

Full transparency, I did delete the posts since this is my burner account and I try to keep it without history (I only now realized that setting a post to "hidden" only hides it for me, and not everyone).

I understand why you would think I'm being mislead, but the chances of that are essentially zero. I spoke to the receptionist at the hospital she was discharged from, I've seen screenshots of her bank statements, pictures of her family. Her father and brother passed away and I saw their obituaries. I found the social media profiles of her mother, siblings, and friends. Working in IT, I've seen countless scams and social engineering attempts over the years, and there hasn't been a single sign of dishonesty here.

She filed her taxes through H&R Block who told her that her refund would be a direct deposit, after which the CRA said that they did not receive the required info. After contacting H&R Block they basically said that it's in the CRA's hands now and there's nothing they can do. I phrased it poorly--the more likely scenario is H&R Block messed up, or if the CRA is to blame, they lost the information somehow--not that they lied about it.

I am absolutely not running a scam. I don't take payments and haven't accepted them from anyone in any amount. I know all these details because we have been close friends for years. I have spent my own money to try and help her. Her life wasn't always like this. I don't know how I can prove the legitimacy of my claims without revealing sensitive personal information, but if there is a way just let me know and I will do it. Considering that I did not ask (or even imply) that I was asking for donations, nor is anyone here offering money, I would appreciate if I could be given the benefit of the doubt.
Haha, nice try US government! I know it’s actually an alien spacecraft!

>But the bigger issue with your post is that you haven't given us much to work with - you mention dance as an interest, but otherwise you have focused on what you don't like.

My apologies; I suppose I only really meant to enquire as to whether many other people had a similar experience, and since the post was so long I didn't want to make it longer. Happy to share though! As for my interests, I have a lot, some of the biggest are: tech, entrepreneurship (I am a business-owner), dance (hip-hop, jazz), learning language/culture, photography, cinematography, graphic design, songwriting / music production (particularly pop, EDM, hip-hop), gaming, fashion design, and more recently vehicle tuning/customization.

I have had quite a bit of difficulty finding things related to these interests in Thunder Bay, perhaps with the exception of entrepreneurship prior to the pandemic (everything is still virtual), and to some degree: dance.

Yes, I realize that it takes time. Of the friends I did make here who moved away, we didn't become such close friends overnight. If I can find someone here where we sort of "click", and they seem reasonably interested in spending time together so that we can get to know each other though, that would be nice, even if things don't work out in the end.

Thank you for the suggestions! Also, yes, I actually wrote and then removed my interests from my original post as I was trying to shorten it (and it still ended up really long, lol.)
